content.headline: Interpreter is now a scaled, reliable asset inside Teams

content.speaker_intent: Have leaders internalize that Interpreter is no longer experimental; it is a scaled, high‑reliability capability worth investing behind.

sections.title: Adoption and Engagement

bullets.text: 136k monthly active Interpreter users (+1.9% MoM) and 106k meetings per month (+5.4% MoM) show sustained demand.
62.2% of Interpreter meetings run longer than 5 minutes (+2.1% MoM), indicating deeper engagement and real meeting dependence.
Retention holds in the 11–13% range, with usage trending up rather than spiking and dropping.

sections.title: Reliability and Quality Foundation

bullets.text: End‑to‑end Interpreter reliability is 99.38% (+0.2% MoM), meeting enterprise expectations for mission‑critical meetings.
Transcript quality improvements reduce Copilot and Recap DSAT by improving readability and entity accuracy at no additional CoGS.
Admin reporting and metering workstreams are underway, laying the foundation for value articulation to enterprise buyers.

story: Situation: link speech quality directly to Teams AI and customer outcomes

content.headline: Unified speech quality is a force multiplier for Teams AI
content.subtitle: Interpreter, captions, and transcription quality directly drive Copilot outcomes and enterprise AI value
content.speaker_intent: Make leaders see speech not as a feature silo but as core infrastructure for Teams AI and enterprise trust.

sections.title: In‑Meeting Experience Drives Perceived Product Value

bullets.text: Multilingual STT with auto language detection removes setup friction and reduces gibberish, especially in bilingual global meetings.
SIM Interpreter improvements (semantic mode, faster TTS) improve flow and reduce latency, aligning better with spoken content.
High reliability (~99%+) makes Interpreter viable for formal, high‑stakes meetings rather than just informal calls.

sections.title: Post‑Meeting AI Relies on Accurate Transcripts and Entities

bullets.text: Transcript Enricher already enhances 1.8M+ meetings weekly, reducing entity errors and accent/dialect issues.
Post‑meeting Enricher cuts inaccuracy from 19.5% to 12.3% (−37%) and boosts CSAT from 42.95% to 62.32%.
Improved entity accuracy directly reduces Copilot and Recap DSAT by grounding AI on cleaner, enriched transcripts.

story: Complication: surface the unresolved pain and risk as a crisis of inaction
visual_design: Problem tree: root = “Multilingual high‑stakes meetings”; three branches = Accuracy, Flow/Tone, Governance/Visibility; bullets under each.

content.headline: Current gaps risk losing high‑stakes multilingual meetings to competitors
content.subtitle: Precision, flow, tone, and governance issues block us from being the default choice for global enterprises
content.speaker_intent: Create constructive anxiety that without decisive investment, we under‑serve the most valuable meetings and weaken our AI differentiation.

sections.title: Accuracy and Domain Precision Still Fall Short

bullets.text: Customers report accuracy issues on technical terms, names, and numbers/units; JP‑EN name recall remains below 50% (improving but not solved).
Simultaneous translations can feel too literal, eroding trust in high‑stakes or public sector settings.
Global dictionary integration is pending and custom dictionaries are still Tier‑1 only, limiting enterprise domain adaptation.

sections.title: Meeting Flow and Tone Can Break Executive‑Level Experiences

bullets.text: Latency and mis‑segmentation in SIM disrupt conversation flow and alignment with shared content; first‑sentence delays are highly sensitive.
Tone and naturalness in JP/KR are not yet market‑grade, with occasional gender/voice mismatches and rare harassment/tone issues.
SIM is better for fluid conversations, but customers lack clear guidance or UX cues for when to use SIM vs Turn‑by‑Turn.

sections.title: Governance and Visibility Limit Enterprise‑Wide Adoption

bullets.text: Cross‑tenant/guest licensing behavior is not clear to customers, creating friction for external or public events.
Interpreted audio is not yet captured in recordings, preventing full meeting parity and compliance in regulated sectors.
Admin reporting and CFR data pipelines are still maturing, limiting how field and admins can articulate value by meeting type and language pair.

story: Question → Answer: introduce the unified speech stack as the strategic response (punchline #1)

content.headline: A unified multilingual speech stack turns pain points into a defensible moat
content.subtitle: One stack for Interpreter, Captions, and Transcription with entity accuracy and governance at the core
content.speaker_intent: Land the core thesis: convergence into a unified speech intelligence layer is how Teams wins global, AI‑driven collaboration.

sections.title: Strategic Question We Are Answering

bullets.text: How do we convert fragmented speech features into a single, AI‑ready speech intelligence layer that delights users, satisfies IT, and differentiates Teams?

sections.title: Our Answer: Unified Speech Intelligence for Teams

bullets.text: Converge Interpreter, Captions, and Transcription onto a unified multilingual STT and enrichment stack, with entity accuracy as the north star.
Pair two complementary Interpreter modes—SIM for fluid conversations and Turn‑by‑Turn for structured meetings—on top of this shared stack.
Wrap the stack with governance, admin reporting, and responsible AI guardrails to make it enterprise‑grade and difficult to replicate.

story: Answer: deep dive on Interpreter SIM + TBT as the flagship experience
visual_design: Side‑by‑side comparison table (Harvey Balls) for SIM vs TBT: columns = SIM, TBT; rows = Use case fit, Flow, Tone, Latency, Accuracy, Status. Below, small timeline for recent and upcoming milestones.

content.headline: Dual‑mode Interpreter combines SIM and Turn‑by‑Turn for every meeting type
content.subtitle: Quality, latency, and tone improvements make Interpreter viable for both fluid and formal conversations
content.speaker_intent: Show that we have a concrete, feasible Interpreter roadmap that directly addresses customer pain and opens premium scenarios.

sections.title: Simultaneous Interpreter (SIM) — Fluid Conversation at Scale

bullets.text: Semantic mode enabled in lower rings and phrase segmentation fixes improve long‑segment coherence and readability.
TTS acceleration (1.2×–1.35×) and audio prefix reduce accumulated translated audio latency and mask first‑turn RTT.
SIM is enabled across Calling and MTR rings with ~99%+ reliability and CSS meeting‑level license checks live.
Phi‑4‑based streaming translation and LM‑based segmentation scoring are under exploration to further improve semantic preservation.

sections.title: Turn‑by‑Turn Interpreter (TBT) — Clarity for High‑Stakes Meetings

bullets.text: R0 is available with early JP/KR customer and GBB feedback citing strong accuracy and clearer turn‑taking.
GPT‑4o‑realtime + Azure Voice Live API stack improves semantic and tone accuracy compared to SIM in structured settings.
Designed for board meetings, lectures, and public sector use (e.g., Welsh Government), where overlapping speech is costly.
Known limits (25 concurrent sessions, some edge cases) are targeted for capacity expansion and stabilization in the next 1–2 quarters.

sections.title: Near‑Term Enhancements (Next 1–2 Quarters)

bullets.text: Expand TBT capacity and harden edge‑case behaviors to support larger events and complex meetings.
Introduce UX cues for turn etiquette and future automatic mode guidance (SIM vs TBT) based on meeting type.
Implement evaluation pipelines for accuracy, tone, and flow, leveraging LLM‑based end‑to‑end metrics for faster iteration.

story: Answer: deep dive on Multilingual STT and Transcript Enricher as the quality engine (punchline #2)
visual_design: Layered process flow (Sankey): Audio → Multilingual STT → Transcript Enricher (real‑time & post‑meeting) → Copilot/Recap/Facilitator; annotations with key metrics (recall, error reduction, CSAT).

content.headline: Multilingual STT and Enricher turn noisy speech into AI‑ready transcripts
content.subtitle: Unified recognition plus entity enrichment materially lift accuracy, CSAT, and Copilot outcomes
content.speaker_intent: Demonstrate that we have a working, scaling quality engine that converts speech into trustworthy artifacts at scale.

sections.title: Multilingual STT — One Endpoint, Less Friction, Better Accuracy

bullets.text: Unified multi‑recognizer endpoint with auto language detection is deployed for R0/R1, supporting 9 languages in preview.
Multilingual STT eliminates setup friction and reduces gibberish, enabling bilingual meetings for global customers.
Entity recall improvements (65.42 → 74.76 Type II) and phrase hint fixes (>800ms freeze) improve both accuracy and responsiveness.

sections.title: Transcript Enricher — Entity‑First Quality Gains at Scale

bullets.text: R4 rollout at 50% for EN/JP and 10% for FR/DE/PT/ES, enhancing 1.8M+ meetings weekly with strong online reliability.
Post‑meeting Enricher reduces overall inaccuracy from 19.5% to 12.3% (−37%) and entity errors by 34%, while cutting accent/dialect issues by 31%.
CSAT jumps from 42.95% to 62.32%, proving that entity‑focused corrections directly improve perceived quality.

sections.title: Roadmap to Full Multilingual and Enterprise Coverage

bullets.text: Multilingual Enricher support planned for CY2026 Q1, with alignment to in‑meeting enrichment architecture.
Tenant auto‑dictionary and broader language coverage (zh‑TW, NL, VI, TH) will further reduce domain errors.
zh‑TW transcription/captioning already treated like zh‑CN at the STT layer, with internal testing planned and Cantonese tracked under Tier‑2 expansion.

story: Answer: position Transcription++ and unified evaluation as the moat and feasibility proof

content.headline: Transcription++ and LLM evaluation make our speech stack hard to copy
content.subtitle: Enterprise understanding, governance‑by‑design, and unified metrics create a durable competitive edge
content.speaker_intent: Reassure leaders that we are building not just features but a defensible platform with built‑in governance and evaluation.

sections.title: Transcription++ — Enterprise Understanding Layer on Top of STT

bullets.text: Tiered model stack with grounding and enrichment converts raw transcripts into enterprise‑aware artifacts.
Global and custom dictionaries plus dynamic vocabulary align speech output with each tenant’s domain language.
Governance‑by‑design and multilingual‑by‑default architecture make it suitable for regulated and global customers.

sections.title: Unified Evaluation — LLM‑as‑Judge for Faster, Safer Rollouts

bullets.text: LLM‑based evaluation produces semantic, tone, latency, and entity scores across ST, Semantic, Phi, GPT‑4o realtime, TBT, and Multilingual STT.
Consistent metrics across models reduce human evaluation cost and accelerate iteration and rollout decisions.
End‑to‑end evaluation enables stronger quality gates and ringed rollout, lowering the risk of regressions in production.

sections.title: Infrastructure — Multi‑Recognizer and GPU Foundation

bullets.text: Multi‑recognizer platform (coming Jan 2026) enables hot‑switching between STS and LRM/LLM models in the same pipeline.
This foundation supports Phi‑4, multimodal LLMs, and unified multilingual models without re‑architecting the product.
Resource expansion (10→20 environments) and robust error handling/retry logic are planned to strengthen global reliability.

story: Answer: connect roadmap to business outcomes and admin value (punchline #3)

content.headline: Next 6–12 months convert technical progress into enterprise‑visible value
content.subtitle: Roadmap focuses on CSAT, governance, language coverage, and recording parity to unlock more revenue‑critical meetings
content.speaker_intent: Show that we have a concrete, time‑bound plan to turn the stack into visible value for customers, field, and leadership.

sections.title: Experience and CSAT Outcomes

bullets.text: Target >80% CSAT for Interpreter by pairing SIM for fluid conversations with TBT for structured clarity and future automatic mode switching.
Improve first‑sentence telemetry, segmentation, and pipeline tuning to reduce perceived latency and flow breaks.
Market‑specific tone tuning for JP/KR to address naturalness and gender/voice concerns in key markets.

sections.title: Governance, Admin Visibility, and Recording Parity

bullets.text: Admin Center usage dashboard preview targeted for Mar 31, 2026, enabling tenant‑level adoption and language pair reporting.
CFR and metering integration to articulate usage by meeting type and support enterprise governance policies.
Recording parity for interpreted audio, including multi‑track options, to satisfy compliance and replay scenarios.

sections.title: Language Coverage and Offline Scenarios

bullets.text: Broaden language coverage to zh‑TW, NL, VI, and TH while continuing Tier‑2 expansion (e.g., Cantonese).
Explore offline and fast catch‑up transcription to support low‑connectivity or late‑join scenarios.
Extend Enricher GA across Tier‑1 languages with multilingual support and tenant auto‑dictionary capabilities.

sections.title: Infrastructure and Model Capacity

bullets.text: Risk: GPU capacity and substrate LLM onboarding timelines could slow real‑time model rollout (Phi‑4, GPT‑4o realtime, multilingual models).
Ask: Prioritize GPU allocation and LLM onboarding for real‑time speech scenarios to maintain latency and quality commitments.

sections.title: Data, Monitoring, and CFR Ownership

bullets.text: Risk: Single points of failure and immature error‑handling/incident monitoring could erode reliability in new environments.
Risk: CFR data cooking ownership and latency are not yet fully resolved, slowing admin reporting and value articulation.
Ask: Clarify CFR data ownership and fund monitoring/alerting maturity to support ringed rollout and admin dashboards.

sections.title: Responsible AI and Market‑Specific Tone

bullets.text: Risk: Harassment/misgendering and tone issues (especially JP/KR) could damage trust in sensitive markets and public sector deployments.
Ask: Endorse stronger Responsible AI guardrails, tone control workstreams, and explicit evaluation criteria for high‑risk locales.
